answer:
Boiled egg yolks are a modest protein source—about **2.4 – 2.7 g of protein per yolk** (depending on egg size).  
Using that range:

| # of yolks | Protein per yolk | Total protein |
|------------|------------------|---------------|
| 1          | 2.4 – 2.7 g      | 2.4 – 2.7 g   |
| 2          | 2.4 – 2.7 g      | 4.8 – 5.4 g   |
| 3          | 2.4 – 2.7 g      | 7.2 – 8.1 g   |
| 4          | 2.4 – 2.7 g      | **9.6 – 10.8 g** |

So, **four boiled egg yolks contain roughly 10 g of protein**, give or take around a gram depending on the exact size of the eggs. If you need a more precise figure for a specific brand or egg size, you can weigh the yolks (average yolk ≈ 15–17 g) and multiply by about 0.16 g of protein per gram of yolk.
